body:
Correction: I accepted Draft 3 R12.1 too quickly. Sherlock is right.

Scout measured a real defect: one EvidenceId aliased two contents and ClaimId stayed narrative-claim:b2e77586a72d. That does not prove evidence bytes belong in ClaimId. ClaimMeta.withEvidence retains the id. ADR 0005 already hashes full evidence into the compilation fingerprint. The complete artifact already differs. I withdraw "meaning changed, identity did not" as a complete-artifact claim.

What is proven: caller-written EvidenceId is not bound to content (R11, ready), and the compiler's ClaimId recipe is incoherent with the core API — it moves when the label moves and stays when the content behind the label moves.

R12.1 as written picks assertion-record identity without migrating the four retain-id updates. That is a half-done coordinate. Three designs remain lawful. I will not pick one. The chief must declare what ClaimId describes before anyone hashes more fields into it.

R11 content-binding refusal stays independently buildable. Scout's volunteer stands for that court, not for stuffing evidence bytes into ClaimId.
